Maria (runtime): Heads-up — nightly perf run shows a weird spike when we transition from prefill -> decode on the paged + FlashAttention-fused variant. p95 latency doubles on small interactive workloads. Not sure if it's KV page thrash or kernel selector oscillation.

benchbot: nightly/2026-03-16 02:15 UTC — model=redwood-xl-8k, mode=interactive
  prefill p50=68ms p95=210ms
  decode p50=9ms p95=420ms  <-- big tail
  tokens/sec(prefill)=3200 tokens/s tokens/sec(decode)=150 tokens/s
  gpu_util=72% mem_rss=9.8G

Cheng: @Maria can you share the exact bench command and kernel flags? also flamegraph/nvprof dump if possible. :thinking:

Maria (runtime): run: `python infra/bench/run.py --model redwood-xl-8k --mode interactive --seq 64 --batch 1 --kernel auto --prefill_tokens 64 --decode_tokens 64`
Attached small log snippet: 
```
[01:12:03] kernel_select: selected=flash_paged_fused v=2
[01:12:03] kvcache: pages_in_use=12 probe_evictions=3
[01:12:06] kernel_select: fallback_to_prefill_kernel=true reason=kv_probe_thrash
[01:12:06] decode_latency_ms=421
```

Sam: sounds like oscillation: selector picks flash_paged_fused for prefill, then decode runs small-batch and triggers kvpage probes which make selector fallback to prefill kernel mid-session. That fallback pays a huge tail. We saw similar on a different model but with bigger batches.

Cheng: can you repro with `--batch 1 --seq 8` (super small) and dump `KERNEL_DEBUG=1`? want to see decision calls. Also what is kvpage eviction threshold now?

Maria (runtime): repro command + debug env: `KERNEL_DEBUG=1 RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=auto python infra/bench/run.py --model redwood-xl-8k --mode decode --batch 1 --seq 8`
Debug excerpt: 
```
[DEBUG] decision: prefill_kernel_score=0.87 decode_kernel_score=0.51
[DEBUG] kvprobe: pages=5 probes=11 latency=3.2ms
[DEBUG] selector: switching to prefill_kernel to reduce probe pressure
```

benchbot: quick microbench (no streaming):
  auto selector p95=410ms
  force decode_fused_small p95=37ms
  force prefill_kernel p95=390ms

Sam: that's telling — the fusion decode kernel handles tiny token decode much better. The selector's scoring function seems too greedy about prefill-cost reuse and not considering small-batch decode tail.

Cheng: proposal: add a small-batch override in selector: if decode and batch<=2 and decode_seq<=16 prefer decode_fused unless kvpages>threshold. Also throttle kvprobe frequency (backoff).

Maria (runtime): quick A/B test: set `RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=prefer_decode_small` on one canary node and ran 1000 interactive sessions: p95 drop from 420ms -> 48ms, error rate unchanged.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: canary-id=canary-20260316-17 node-set=interactive-small-1 pct=5 duration=30m

Sam: nice. Next steps:
- Cheng to add selector heuristic PR (small-batch override + probe backoff).
- Maria to add microbench to CI that includes prefill->decode handoff case (batch=1, seq=8/64).
- I'll add telemetry for kernel switches per-session (so we can alert if oscillation > x/min).

Cheng: I'll open PR today. Also adding a feature flag `selector.force_decode_small=true` to test ramp.

Maria (runtime): PR #? once CI green I'll flip flag on canary. thanks all :thumbsup:

benchbot: note — saved raw flamegraph to s3://redwood-bench/nightly/2026-03-16/flame-1839998888.html

Sam: let's watch the canary metrics; if p95 stays low for 30m we roll to 25%. If not, rollback and we'll iterate on probe backoff.

Cheng: also adding a unit test for kernel scoring math to prevent regressions.

Maria (runtime): filing a short incident ticket to track: INF-2026-394 (root cause hypothesis: selector mis-weight for small decode vs kvprobe cost).

ops-bot: action items assigned: Cheng (add selector heuristic), Maria (bench CI + ticket), Sam (telemetry + canary monitor).
